# Changelog

What changed in each release, newest first. Breaking changes are marked **Breaking**.

## v1.15.1

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-26" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.15.0...v1.15.1" kind="compare" />

### ThemeToggle

- Fixed `ThemeScript` shipping as a client component. It renders a constant and needs nothing from the client, so the `"use client"` directive is gone. In a Next.js App Router layout it is now a plain server component that sends no JS, and `themeInitScript` reaches server code as the string itself instead of a client reference.

### General

- Fixed the `@forte-ui/react` barrel being one client entry (#165). It no longer carries `"use client"`. The boundary is each component's own module, so `import { Button } from "@forte-ui/react"` in a React Server Component still works. A server layout that imported only `ThemeScript` used to send every component's JS and stylesheet to every page of a Next.js app. Per-page JS in those apps now roughly halves, and server-safe values such as `DEFAULT_SWATCHES` reach server code as values rather than client references.
- Changed how component CSS ships. All component styles are now one `dist/styles/components.css`, pulled in by the published `@forte-ui/react/theme.css`, and the per-component CSS the JS used to inject is gone (`vite-plugin-lib-inject-css` is dropped). Apps that already import `@forte-ui/react/theme.css` need no change. In Next.js App Router apps, per-page stylesheets go from one per component to a small constant set, and the "import `globals.css` before `@forte-ui/react`" ordering requirement no longer applies. Vite apps lose per-component CSS tree-shaking: about 48 KB gzipped of component CSS now ships whatever a page renders.

### create-forte-ui

- Changed the Next.js + Tailwind layout template to stop emitting the "globals.css first" warning comment above its imports. The ordering it warned about no longer matters now that component CSS arrives through `theme.css`.

## v1.15.0

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-22" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.14.2...v1.15.0" kind="compare" />

### ColorPicker

- Added "no color" support: `value={null}` keeps the picker controlled and empty, and `defaultValue={null}` starts an uncontrolled picker empty. Before, `undefined` was the only way to say a value was unset, and it makes the picker uncontrolled, so an optional color (an outline, a border, a text background) needed a stand-in like `#000000`, and the picker then showed black as picked. While empty, no swatch is ticked, the `ColorPicker.Input` is blank with the empty label as its placeholder, the area and rail handles are hidden until they take keyboard focus, `ColorPicker.Value` shows the empty label, and the trigger swatch and `ColorPicker.Preview` draw a slash instead of a color. `ColorPicker.HiddenInput` submits an empty string, not the last color worked in. The first pick emits a color as usual. Switching the format while empty emits nothing, and a remembered black, gray or transparent seeds the first pick at full color so a hue drag is visible. `value` and `defaultValue` are now typed `string | null`.
- Added the `emptyLabel` prop on `ColorPicker.Root` (default `"None"`): the text that stands in for a color while `value` is `null`. It is the input's placeholder, `ColorPicker.Value`'s text, and what the trigger and the handles announce to assistive technology.
- Added the `data-empty` attribute, set while no color is picked, on the trigger, the trigger swatch, the popup panel, `ColorPicker.Panel`, the area, the hue and alpha sliders, `ColorPicker.Preview`, `ColorPicker.Value` and `ColorPicker.Input`, so an empty picker can be styled from plain CSS.
- Added the `--forte-color-picker-empty-mark` theming knob, the color of the slash drawn in the preview and the trigger swatch while no color is set. It defaults to `--forte-color-danger`.

## v1.14.2

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-20" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.14.1...v1.14.2" kind="compare" />

### Combobox

- Fixed a `multiple` field growing past its control height when it held a chip. At `sm` the field is 18px inside, but a chip was 24px at every size (block padding around its 16px remove button), so one chip took the field from 28px to 34px. A chip now has a height instead of padding: 24px where the field has room, and the field's inner height where it does not.
- Fixed Clear and Trigger moving to a row of their own when chips wrapped. The chips container sized itself from its max-content width, which counts the input at its default width (about 156px), so two short chips outgrew the room beside the buttons. It now takes only the room the buttons leave and wraps inside itself, and the buttons are pinned to the first row, so a field whose chips wrap keeps its caret where a one-row field has it. At a narrow `sm` width (256px) the input can still take a second row, because the two chips plus the input's 64px minimum need more room than the buttons leave. The buttons stay on the first row.
- Fixed every `compact` `sm` field (24px) rendering a fraction taller than its control height, and a chip growing it by 10px.
- Added the `--forte-combobox-field-py` theming knob, the field's block padding. It defaults to `--forte-space-1`, capped so the inside still holds a 16px glyph: 3px at `compact` `sm`, and the full `--forte-space-1` at every other size and density. The button size, button radius and chip radius read it.

## v1.14.1

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-20" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.14.0...v1.14.1" kind="compare" />

### InputGroup

- Fixed an `sm` group growing past its control height when an icon-only button sat in an addon. A search field with a clear button went from 28px to 34px the moment the button appeared, because Button's `iconOnly` rule floors its box at the 24px target on both axes and the group only reset the width floor. The height floor now comes down to the field too; the button's hit area stays at the 24px `--forte-target-min`. `md` and `lg` were not affected.
- Fixed a `compact` `sm` group (24px) growing for every kind of addon content, including text, icons and icon-only buttons. `--forte-input-group-py` now defaults to `--forte-space-1` capped to what leaves room for an icon-only button: 2px at `compact` `sm`, and unchanged (`--forte-space-1`) at every other size and density.

## v1.14.0

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-17" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.13.2...v1.14.0" kind="compare" />

### Design tokens & motion

- Added `--forte-color-selection` (accent step 6) and `--forte-color-on-selection` (accent step 12), the pair every field paints its selected text in. Step 12 on step 6 is asserted by the contrast harness at 4.5:1 (worst case 7.48:1 light, 5.66:1 dark).

### General

- Fixed selected text being nearly invisible in `Input`, `Textarea`, `InputGroup`, `NumberField`, `OTPField` and `Combobox`. The selection was painted on the soft accent step, which sat as little as 1.11:1 off the page in light mode and 1.23:1 in dark, so a selection read as the value changing color rather than as a highlight. It now paints on `--forte-color-selection` with `--forte-color-on-selection` text. This matters most in `OTPField`, where every slot selects its character on focus. The selection knobs default to the new tokens: `--forte-input-selection-bg` / `-fg`, `--forte-textarea-selection-bg` / `-fg`, `--forte-input-group-selection-bg` / `-fg`, `--forte-number-field-input-selection-bg` / `-fg` and `--forte-otp-field-selection-bg` / `-fg` (`Combobox` has none).
- Added `bg-selection` and `text-on-selection` to the `@forte-ui/react/tailwind.css` bridge (`--color-selection`, `--color-on-selection`), so a field of your own can match the library's: `selection:bg-selection selection:text-on-selection`.

## v1.13.2

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-17" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.13.1...v1.13.2" kind="compare" />

### ToggleGroup

- Fixed a `segmented` ToggleGroup strip whose corners did not match the toggles inside it. The strip's radius was a fixed `--forte-radius-4`, so under the `soft`, `pill` and `none` radius presets the toggles sat in a track of the wrong curvature, and even at the default the strip was off by the padding. The radius is now derived from the toggles' radius (`--forte-radius-control`) plus the padding and border around them, so the two stay concentric under every preset. The `none` preset keeps a square strip. `--forte-toggle-group-radius` now defaults to that derived value when `segmented`. If you re-point the toggles' radius on the toggles themselves, set this knob alongside it, because the group cannot see a knob declared on each toggle.

## v1.13.1

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-16" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.13.0...v1.13.1" kind="compare" />

### Drawer

- Fixed a non-modal drawer (`modal={false}` or `modal="trap-focus"`) blocking the page behind it. The scrim used to catch every press aimed at the page, even at the lowest snap point where it is fully transparent and the page looks usable. In these modes the scrim is now purely visual and lets presses through, so they reach the page and Base UI's outside-press dismissal alike. The backdrop is marked `data-non-modal` while this applies. A drawer that turns modal as it is raised takes presses again from that render on.
- Fixed the receded page showing square corners behind `Drawer.Indent`. An app shell's first child, usually a painted app bar flush with the top, covered the rounded corners. The active indent now clips its contents to the radius. The clip is held until the return transition finishes, so the corners do not square off while the radius is still easing out. Nothing changes at rest. While a drawer is open, anything that draws past the indent's box without a portal, such as a shadow or an unportalled popover, is cut at its edge.

## v1.13.0

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-16" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.12.1...v1.13.0" kind="compare" />

### Drawer

- Added the indent effect, which pushes the app back while a drawer is open, the way a native sheet does. `Drawer.Provider` renders no element and reports whether any drawer inside it is open. `Drawer.Indent` wraps the app's UI and recedes: it scales down, drops a step and rounds its top corners, easing back to rest in step with a dismissing drag. `Drawer.IndentBackground` is the decorative fixed layer, transparent until a drawer opens, that shows around the receded page. Put the background directly before the indent inside the same provider. The exports are `DrawerProvider`, `DrawerIndent` and `DrawerIndentBackground`, with `DrawerProviderProps`, `DrawerIndentProps` and `DrawerIndentBackgroundProps` as types.
- Keep `position: fixed` chrome, such as a fixed header, outside `Drawer.Indent`. While a drawer is open the indent is transformed, so its fixed descendants stop following the viewport. At rest nothing is transformed, so the indent has no effect on fixed elements.
- Added theming knobs for the indent: `--forte-drawer-indent-bg`, `--forte-drawer-indent-scale`, `--forte-drawer-indent-travel`, `--forte-drawer-indent-radius`, `--forte-drawer-indent-duration`, `--forte-drawer-indent-ease`, `--forte-drawer-indent-exit-duration` and `--forte-drawer-indent-exit-ease`. The background part has `--forte-drawer-indent-background-color`. The page does not scale or round under reduced motion, because the scale and radius are gated on motion. The new parts carry `data-forte="drawer-indent"` and `data-forte="drawer-indent-background"`.
- Changed the hairline border so it is drawn on all four sides of every drawer. An `edge` drawer previously drew it only on the side facing into the page. During an overdrag the outer side now shows as a line between the surface and the skirt beyond it. A drawer with another drawer open over it still has its whole ring painted in the scrim color. `--forte-drawer-border-width` now applies to all four sides.
- Added `hairline` to `Drawer.Popup` (default `true`). Pass `hairline={false}` to drop the line, for a surface separated by its shadow and the scrim alone. The popup is then marked `data-no-hairline`. The border is made transparent rather than zero-width, so nothing shifts and forced-colors mode keeps its system-colored boundary. Use this instead of setting `--forte-drawer-border-width` to `0px`, which would remove that boundary too.

## v1.12.1

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-15" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.12.0...v1.12.1" kind="compare" />

### Drawer

- Every drawer now draws a hairline border, not just one with `backdrop={false}`. An `edge` drawer draws it only on the side that faces into the page. The other three sides stay transparent, so an overdrag does not expose a seam against the bezel. A `floating` drawer draws all four sides. A drawer with another drawer open over it still has its whole ring painted in the scrim color, so a receding parent gets no bright outline. `--forte-drawer-border-width` and `--forte-drawer-border-color` now apply to every drawer.
- `data-no-backdrop` is still set on the popup when `backdrop={false}`. Nothing in the stylesheet reads it any more, so it is now only a hook for styling scrimless drawers.

## v1.12.0

<ReleaseMeta date="2026-10-10" href="https://github.com/arsen/forte-ui/compare/v1.11.3...v1.12.0" kind="compare" />

### Carousel

- Added `onSettle` to `Carousel.Root`. It is called with the index and the change reason once the track has come to rest on a slide, after the glide that a drag, a control, autoplay or a clamp started, or on the next frame when there is no glide. A glide that a drag catches or another move retargets never settles, and only the last one is reported. Use it for work that would stall the glide, such as mounting something heavy for the new slide, instead of `onIndexChange`, which fires on release.
- Added a `data-settling` attribute on the carousel root. It is present from the moment a move starts until the track has settled, and is absent while dragging. It lets plain CSS style the in-between state.
